Who we serve
scope of application
join the project
LifeguardEye delivers adaptable, AI-powered oversight for every aquatic environment — from small community pools to large water parks, open water, and professional rescue missions.
LifeguardEye enhances safety in high-responsibility environments where consistent supervision is critical.
Public & Community Pools
Water Parks & Recreational Centers
Open Water & Public Waterfronts
Patrol & Rescue Missions
Water parks present unique safety challenges due to crowd density and constant movement.
Open water conditions change constantly — visibility, currents, waves, and crowd behavior are less predictable.
Beyond fixed facilities, LifeguardEye can operate as a mobile situational-awareness tool. It supports search, rescue, and patrol missions where quick detection and reliable visual analysis are critical.
  • real-time detection of dangerous situations;
  • automated oversight of deep water, children’s areas, and high-risk zones;
  • actionable daily reports for managers and risk-management teams.
Key benefits:
  • monitoring of large, complex, and fast-moving environments;
  • reliable performance despite splashes, foam, glare, or inconsistent lighting;
  • early detection of critical behaviors among large groups of guests.
Key benefits:
  • real-time behavior analysis on and near the water;
  • support for lifeguards in low-visibility or high-risk conditions;
  • early warning of potentially dangerous scenarios.
Key benefits:
  • real-time video analysis from mobile cameras, temporary setups, or drones;
  • assistance in locating individuals and identifying unusual or risky behavior;
  • effective performance in non-standard, challenging environments.
Key benefits:
AI-powered continuous surveillance that maintains full situational awareness across the entire aquatic environment — day and night.
24/7 Intelligent Monitoring
Monitors each zone independently —shallow water, deep areas, lap lanes, or restricted sections — while detecting overcrowding and unusual activity patterns.
Zone-Based Oversight & Crowd Awareness
Immediate audio notifications sent directly to lifeguard devices, enabling faster response and reducing the risk of missed incidents.
Instant Alerts to Lifeguards
Automatically identifies prolonged submersion, lack of movement, or other early indicators of distress to help prevent critical situations.
Real-Time Behavior & Submersion Detection

advantages
Safety & Operational Impact
LifeguardEye delivers detailed analytics on visitor flow and zone activity. This operational data empowers managers to optimize staffing, reduce congestion, enhance the guest experience, and plan programs with confidence.
Visitor Flow & Occupancy Analytics
The system highlights risk factors before they escalate into dangerous situations. This includes detecting swimmers entering high-risk zones, identifying prolonged underwater presence, spotting isolated swimmers, and recognizing early signs of fatigue or distress.
Early-Risk Identification & Hazard Prevention
LifeguardEye provides structured reports that help leadership understand real risk patterns — visitor behavior, near-miss events, and staff response times.
These insights support data-driven decisions in staffing, training, scheduling, and long-term safety improvements.
Actionable Analytics for Risk Management & Training
LifeguardEye strengthens on-site supervision by enhancing human observation with continuous AI oversight. It helps lifeguards maintain focus, reduces cognitive load, and supports them in visually complex or high-traffic environments — improving safety without replacing staff.
A safer and more controlled aquatic environment increases visitor confidence and satisfaction. Families, swimmers, and athletes feel more secure knowing the facility uses advanced AI protection — strengthening the facility’s reputation, community trust, and public responsibility.
Social Responsibility & Community Impact
Lifeguard Empowerment & Operational Support

Deep & Competitive Pools
Deep & Competitive Pools
  • rapid vertical ascents and descents
  • long underwater sequences
  • strong turbulence
  • multiple athletes performing complex choreography
Deep pools used for synchronized swimming and diving feature:
LifeguardEye has been trained and validated in these exact conditions, gaining the ability to distinguish between high-intensity athletic activity and genuine signs of distress.
This experience forms the foundation for accurate detection in any deep-water scenario.
Competitive aquatic environments are among the most demanding for any vision-based system.
Synchronized swimming, diving, high-performance training
Public Pools & Municipal Facilities
  • varied age groups and skill levels
  • crowds moving in unpredictable patterns
  • sudden jumps, splashes, and playful behavior
  • shifting light conditions throughout the day
  • lanes, recreation zones, free swim, classes — all at once
Public pools present a completely different set of challenges:
Our installations in community and municipal pools taught the AI to interpret highly variable movement patterns, segment zones correctly, and detect prolonged underwater stillness even in visually overloaded settings.

This is where LifeguardEye learned to operate reliably in environments where visibility is often limited and motion is chaotic.
Mixed activities, dynamic lighting, variable crowd density
Multi-Zone Recreation & Family Centers
  • shallow pools with small children
  • inflatable toys, floaters, and visual noise
  • unpredictable behavior and rapid posture changes
  • partial occlusions when children cluster together
Family aquatic centers present some of the most safety-critical scenarios:
These environments forced our AI to learn subtle early indicators of risk that differ significantly from those seen in adult swimmers.
Children’s areas, shallow zones, small objects, fast random motion
Open-Water Testing
  • irregular wave patterns
  • strong reflections from the sun
  • currents and drift
  • variable turbidity and shifting visibility
  • swimmers partially or fully obscured by surface motion
Open-water conditions introduce an entirely new dimension of complexity:
Field tests on beaches allowed us to push the AI beyond controlled pool environments and understand how natural water behaves — how it distorts motion, how it hides early signs of trouble, and how environmental dynamics differ from those in still water.
This experience significantly broadened the robustness of our algorithms.
Beach environments, waves, currents, natural light variability
Aerial & Perimeter Monitoring (Drone-Based Analysis)
  • monitoring large surf areas
  • identifying swimmers drifting into dangerous locations
  • scanning broad coastal zones where traditional cameras cannot reach
Working with aerial video from drones introduced new possibilities:
Drone analysis helped LifeguardEye learn long-range tracking, behavior recognition from overhead angles, and situational understanding across wide, unstructured aquatic areas.

This expertise supports future expansion into large-scale aquatic safety and coastline surveillance.
Surf zones, long-distance tracking, environmental hazards
